title: Heap-Only Tuple (HOT) Optimization Failures and Write Amplification
realWorldScenario: An application updates a `last_seen_at` timestamp on `users` on every API request. Although the table only has 1 million rows, disk write I/O is 80 MB/sec and index size is growing by 5 GB per day. Telemetry shows HOT update ratio is 0%.
questionStatement: Explain PostgreSQL Heap-Only Tuple (HOT) optimization. What are the two mandatory conditions required for an UPDATE to qualify as a HOT update? Why does indexing `last_seen_at` completely disable HOT updates, causing massive write amplification and index bloat?
expectedConcepts: Condition 1: Free space in same 8KB page (fillfactor)
Condition 2: No modified column belongs to any index
Write amplification across all table indexes when HOT fails
hints: What must be true about the columns being updated for HOT to work?
Where must the new row version fit for HOT optimization?
